h: The town that gave us the steam engine
p: Commercial Street is in the heart of Camborne, and you won't be in town long before you spot Richard Trevithick. The Cornish engineer was from here, and his statue stands outside the library on Cross Street. On Christmas Eve 1801 his Puffing Devil steam carriage chugged up Camborne Hill, and the town still celebrates him every spring with Trevithick Day, when steam engines parade through the streets.

Camborne was a big mining town, and the heritage is everywhere. Heartlands, the free attraction on the old Robinson's Shaft site at Pool, is a short drive away, and King Edward Mine has a museum about the area's tin mining. Redruth is just up the road, and the north coast beaches at Portreath are close by.
The Bank Gaming Lounge is 18+, so it's one for the grown-ups.
